recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — reverses_request_id column, model field, repository plumbing
recommended_phases.rationale: Everything downstream needs the column and the field to exist. New knex migration adds nullable `reverses_request_id` (t.string, self-referencing FK to leave_requests.id, plus an index) portable across pg and sqlite3 so `npm run smoke` still runs on a throwaway file DB. `LeaveRequest` gains `reversesRequestId: string | null`; `CreateLeaveRequestInput` is unchanged in shape (still Omit<LeaveRequest,'id'>) so `create` supplies it. `PgLeaveRequestRepository` carries it end-to-end: COLUMNS, LeaveRequestRow, mapRow, and the create INSERT value list. No new repository method and no service change — the existing `create` is the insert path the reversal reuses. Existing rows read back null, so nothing else breaks.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — LeaveService.cancel reversal branch (GP-008)
recommended_phases.rationale: The behavioural core, one file. `cancel(actor, requestId)` keeps its signature and its existing guards (assertCanCancel, the startDate <= today ConflictError). DRAFT and SUBMITTED keep the current in-place `repository.update(requestId, { status: CANCELLED, cancelledBy, cancelledAt })` path untouched — no completed approval exists in those states. APPROVED takes the new branch: the original row is NEVER updated (status, approverId, approvalComment, decidedAt stay immutable); instead `repository.create({ ...original fields, status: CANCELLED, cancelledBy: actor.id, cancelledAt: now, reversesRequestId: requestId })` inserts a NEW row. The balance release is unchanged and still happens exactly once inside the same `uow.withTransaction`: `usedDays -= request.requestedDays` on the ORIGINAL request's requestedDays, with the row read via resolveBalance(..., client, true). The single AuditAction.CANCEL record and the single cancellation notification are still written in that same transaction, with the client threaded through. The returned value is the new CANCELLED row.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — expose reversesRequestId on the read model (wire + web)
recommended_phases.rationale: Keep the wire contract honest: a cancelled-after-approval request is now two rows, so a client must be able to tell which is which. The backend read path needs no code change — `GET /leaves` and `GET /leaves/:id` already serialize the LeaveRequest model, which now carries `reversesRequestId` — but the frontend read model must declare it: `web/src/shared/types/index.ts` `LeaveRequestView` gains `reversesRequestId: string | null`, and `web/src/infrastructure/api/api-client.ts` passes it through unchanged (no mapping layer to update). `web-leave`'s service and actions are untouched. No new endpoint, no new query param.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — tests: reversal unit test + smoke assertion
recommended_phases.rationale: Proves the acceptance criterion. Extend `tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts` with a reversal describe block using the existing in-memory fakes: after cancelling an APPROVED request, assert the original row still reads APPROVED with approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt unchanged (the fake repository must record that no `update` targeted the original id), that exactly one new row was created with status CANCELLED and `reversesRequestId === originalId`, that `usedDays` was released exactly once by the original requestedDays (one balance update, no double release), that exactly one CANCEL audit entry and one notification were written, and that all of it happened inside a single `withTransaction` callback with the stub client forwarded. Also assert the DRAFT/SUBMITTED paths still mutate in place and create no new row. Extend `scripts/smoke.js` with a Postgres-only stage that approves then cancels and asserts two rows with the original still APPROVED.

app_notes:
## Layer boundaries (modular monolith, dependencies flow inward only)

- **Presentation** — `src/modules/*/*.routes.ts` (Fastify route handlers; no controller layer, per the standing decision). Routes do boundary parsing (`parseCreateBody`, `parseQuery`), `resolveActor`, and `sendError`; they contain no business logic and no SQL.
- **Application** — `src/modules/*/*.service.ts` (`ILeaveService`, `IBalanceService`, `IAuditService`, `INotificationService`, `IEmployeeService`, `IPolicyService`, `IValidationService`). Services own the transaction boundary via `IUnitOfWork.withTransaction` and orchestrate repositories. `leave` is the sole orchestrator.
- **Domain** — `src/modules/*/*.model.ts` (entities + `Create*Input` types) and `src/shared/types/index.ts` (canonical enums, cross-module DTOs, `requestedDays`).
- **Infrastructure** — `src/modules/*/*.repository.ts` (`Pg*Repository`), `src/shared/db/` (pool, `PgUnitOfWork`), `migrations/`.

Every public service method is declared on an interface before its implementation (`ILeaveService`, `ILeaveRepository`, `IBalanceRepository`, `IAuditService`, `INotificationService`, `IUnitOfWork`, `IEmployeeService`, `IPolicyService`, `IValidationService`). No implementation is referenced by a consumer except through its interface plus a composition factory (`createLeaveService`, `createPolicyService`).

## Shared value-type placement (applied mechanically)

`reversesRequestId` is a field on the `LeaveRequest` entity, which has owned lifecycle behaviour (DRAFT→SUBMITTED→APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED) and is consumed by exactly one backend module (`leave`). It therefore stays in `src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts` and is **not** promoted to `src/shared/types/`. No new enum or DTO is introduced by this feature, so `src/shared/types/` is unchanged on the backend. On the web root, `LeaveRequestView` is imported by `web-leave`, `web-approvals` and `web-presentation-pages`, so the new field is added to `web/src/shared/types/index.ts` — the shared-types location — not to a single-purpose module.

## GP-008 mechanics (the whole point of the feature)

`cancel(actor, requestId)` keeps one signature and one transaction, and branches on the loaded request's status:

- **DRAFT / SUBMITTED** — unchanged in-place `repository.update(requestId, { status: CANCELLED, cancelledBy, cancelledAt })`. No completed approval exists, so GP-008 does not apply.
- **APPROVED** — the original row is never written. `repository.create({ ...original, status: CANCELLED, cancelledBy: actor.id, cancelledAt: now, reversesRequestId: requestId })` inserts a NEW row. The original's `status`, `approverId`, `approvalComment` and `decidedAt` remain byte-identical.

Balance release is unchanged and happens **exactly once**, in the same `uow.withTransaction`, computed from the ORIGINAL request's `requestedDays`: `usedDays -= requestedDays` via `IBalanceRepository.update`, with the row read through `resolveBalance(..., client, true)` so the row lock is held. The single `AuditAction.CANCEL` record and the single cancellation notification are written in that same transaction with the client threaded through. No new repository method is needed — the existing `create` is the insert path.

## Dependency direction (verified acyclic)

`leave → {shared-types, shared-db, shared-errors, shared-date, balance, audit, notification, validation, employee, policy}`; `balance → {policy, employee, shared-db, shared-date, shared-types}`; `policy → {leave-type, shared-types, shared-db}`; `audit`/`notification`/`employee`/`validation` → shared foundations only. No module depends back on `leave`; `leave` and `balance` no longer import `leave-type` (they reach it through `createPolicyService`). Web root: `web-presentation-pages → web-approvals → web-leave → web-infrastructure-api → web-shared-types`. Every edge is one-directional; no cycle exists.

## Phase ordering

Phases are ordered by dependency: the column/model/repository plumbing (1) must land before the service branch (2) can insert a reversal row; the read-model exposure (3) depends on the model field from (1); tests (4) depend on (1)–(3). Each phase is 1–3 files, well inside Aider's effective context window.

open_questions.question: Which fields does the NEW CANCELLED reversal row copy from the original APPROVED row — the full request shape (employeeId, leaveTypeCode, startDate, endDate, requestedDays, reason) or a minimal tombstone?
open_questions.impact: Determines the read model a client sees for a cancelled-after-approval request and whether the reversal row is self-describing. The balance release math is unaffected either way (it uses the ORIGINAL request's requestedDays), but a tombstone row would make GET /leaves return a row with null dates, which the frontend LeaveRequestView types as non-nullable Date.
candidate_options: Copy the full request shape verbatim (employeeId, leaveTypeCode, startDate, endDate, requestedDays, reason) and set status CANCELLED, cancelledBy, cancelledAt, reversesRequestId — the reversal row is a complete, self-describing request
Copy only identity + linkage (employeeId, leaveTypeCode, requestedDays, reversesRequestId) and leave dates/reason null — requires widening LeaveRequestView dates to nullable

open_questions.question: What should the reversal row's approverId, approvalComment, submittedAt and decidedAt be?
open_questions.impact: GP-008 forbids modifying the original's approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt, but says nothing about the new row's. If the reversal row copies the original approver's identity it reads as if the approver decided the cancellation; if it is null the row carries no decision provenance and the audit log is the only record of who cancelled.
candidate_options: Null approverId/approvalComment/submittedAt/decidedAt on the reversal row; cancelledBy/cancelledAt carry the actor and the CANCEL audit record carries provenance
Copy the original approverId/approvalComment/decidedAt onto the reversal row so the reversal is traceable to the approval it reverses
Set approverId = actor.id and decidedAt = now on the reversal row (treating the cancellation as the reversal row's decision)

open_questions.question: Should GET /leaves return the original APPROVED row and its CANCELLED reversal row as two independent entries, or should the read path collapse/suppress one of them?
open_questions.impact: The feature explicitly exposes reversesRequestId so a client can tell which is which, which implies both rows are returned. But every existing consumer (web LeaveListPage, ApprovalsPage, DashboardPage) will now render two rows for one logical request unless it learns to filter, and the role-scoped visibility rules (EMPLOYEE own / MANAGER direct reports / ADMIN all) apply to both rows identically since they share employeeId.
candidate_options: Return both rows unchanged; clients filter on reversesRequestId (no backend read-path change, no new query param)
Return both rows but add an optional includeReversals query param defaulting to true
Suppress the original APPROVED row when a reversal exists (requires a join/subquery in findByQuery and breaks the immutable-row-is-still-readable contract)

open_questions.question: Can a reversal row itself be cancelled, and can the same APPROVED request be cancelled twice?
open_questions.impact: assertCanCancel currently keys off status only. A CANCELLED reversal row owned by the actor would fall through to the 'only the owner may cancel this leave request' ForbiddenError, which is probably correct, but a second cancel of the same APPROVED original would insert a SECOND reversal row and release usedDays a second time — the double-release the feature explicitly forbids.
candidate_options: Guard in the service: reject cancellation when the target already has a reversal row (requires a repository lookup by reversesRequestId), throwing ConflictError
Rely on the existing status guard only — the original stays APPROVED so a second cancel is currently reachable and would double-release
Add a partial unique index on reverses_request_id so the database rejects a second reversal of the same original

auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: EmployeeRole } where EmployeeRole = 'EMPLOYEE' | 'MANAGER' | 'ADMIN'. Identity and role are obtained from a JWT bearer token verified by the existing registerAuth preHandler (src/shared/auth/index.ts), which populates request.user from payload.sub (id) and payload.role; only '/auth/login' is in PUBLIC_PATHS. RBAC is enforced at the API boundary by the route-level resolveActor helper (throws UnauthorizedError on a missing/invalid actor) and in the service by assertAuthenticated/assertCanCancel/assertCanDecide — never inline in a route handler. This feature adds no new endpoint and no new role: POST /leaves/:id/cancel keeps its existing authorization (owner may cancel own DRAFT/SUBMITTED; only the direct manager or an ADMIN may cancel an APPROVED request; no self-approval), and the new reversal row inherits the original's employeeId, so the existing role-scoped visibility rules (EMPLOYEE own / MANAGER own + direct reports / ADMIN all) apply to it unchanged.
error_response_contract: Errors return { error: string; code: string }. Validation failure -> HTTP 400 (ValidationError, code VALIDATION); authentication failure -> HTTP 401 (UnauthorizedError, code UNAUTHORIZED); authorization failure -> HTTP 403 (ForbiddenError, code FORBIDDEN); not found -> HTTP 404 (NotFoundError, code NOT_FOUND); invalid state transition -> HTTP 409 (ConflictError, code CONFLICT); any other throw -> HTTP 500 { error: 'Internal Server Error' }. GET /leaves/:id returns the same 404 for a request the caller may not see as for one that does not exist. This feature adds no new status code: cancelling an APPROVED request still returns 200 with the new CANCELLED reversal row, and the existing guards (startDate <= today, non-owner, non-direct-manager) keep their current 409/403 responses.
